name: Sift
text: The metadata spec risks over-engineering a one-off transcript merge. name: Scope

name: Scriv
text: The metadata spec risks becoming shelfware—teams will write it, file it, and ignore it when the next urgent transcript lands. Instead, enforce the minimal metadata layer *only* for assets that enter the AI Executive Assistant workflow, starting with the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript. Done when Creative delivers the spec *and* Engineering builds a one-time validator that rejects any asset missing title, speaker, or timestamp.

name: Reel
text: Creative writes a one-page metadata spec—title, speaker, timestamp—then Engineering adds a single validation gate at ingest. This keeps the *Science of Sleep Optimization* merge on track while proving the spec works for one asset. Trade-off: we accept a small delay now to avoid a bigger rework later.

name: Scriv
text: The one-page spec is shelfware bait. Creative will write it, Engineering will bolt on a gate, and the next transcript merge will bypass both—because the AI Executive Assistant pattern already handles speaker/timestamp extraction. Instead, enforce the minimal metadata layer *only* for assets that need downstream reuse, starting with the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript. Done when the transcript is ingested *and* the workflow logs the metadata in the asset’s header.

name: Chisel
text: Creative owns the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript merge into the AI Executive Assistant pattern immediately—no metadata spec, no validation gate. Engineering validates the input once during ingest to confirm speaker/timestamp accuracy. Trade-off: we skip the spec now to avoid a one-sprint delay, but risk inconsistent metadata for future assets.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s plan skips the spec entirely, but that risks inconsistent speaker/timestamp data slipping into the AI Executive Assistant workflow—then we’ll waste more time cleaning up bad inputs later. Instead, Creative writes a one-page spec *only* for the *Science of Sleep Optimization* transcript, and Engineering adds a lightweight validation gate at ingest; if it holds for this asset, we expand it to future transcripts. Settle it by running the merge with the gate and measuring rework hours—if it’s under 2, we keep the spec; if it’s zero, we scrap it.
